n: A new era begins. Moses is gone, and the Lord speaks directly to Joshua, who had served as Moses’ assistant for forty years. His name means “Jehovah saves” — the Hebrew form of the name Jesus.

f.g: Hebrew Yehoshua; Greek Iēsous — the same name as Jesus.

n: God’s message is simple: Moses is dead — now get up and lead the people across the Jordan. Grief gives way to action.
Wherever they walk, God has already given them the land, just as promised to Moses. Their part is to step forward in faith.

f.w: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon

n: The promised borders reach from the southern desert to Lebanon, east to the Euphrates, and west to the Mediterranean.

f.g: Here a general name for Syria and the lands to the north.

n: God promises Joshua what he gave Moses: no one will withstand him, and God will never abandon him.

f.w: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee
as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee

n: The first of three calls to courage. Joshua’s task is to lead Israel in dividing the promised land.

f.w: Be strong and of a good courage

n: Courage is needed most for obedience. Strength here means keeping God’s law without swerving — the true key to success.

f.w: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left

n: Joshua must keep the law on his lips and ponder it day and night. Scripture study is the foundation of prosperity in God’s sense.

f.g: Meditate = murmur or recite quietly while reflecting.

n: “Have I not commanded you?” Courage is a commandment, grounded in the promise that God goes everywhere with us.

f.w: be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed

n: Joshua immediately acts, giving orders to the officers.

f.g: Administrative leaders, perhaps scribes or organizers.

n: Gather food — in three days they will cross the Jordan. Faith includes practical preparation.
Joshua turns to the two and a half tribes that had already received land east of the Jordan.
He reminds them of their promise to Moses: God has given them rest and land.
Their families and herds stay behind, but the warriors must cross armed and help the other tribes.
They can return home only after their brothers also have rest. Covenant people don’t settle down while others still struggle.

f.w: Until the LORD have given your brethren rest

n: The eastern tribes — and all Israel — pledge complete obedience: “Whatever you command, we’ll do; wherever you send, we’ll go.”

f.w: whithersoever thou sendest us, we will go

n: They will follow Joshua as they followed Moses, and they pray that God will be with him in the same way.

f.w: only the LORD thy God be with thee

n: They even back his authority with the strongest penalty, and they echo God’s own words back to him: “Be strong and courageous!”

f.w: only be strong and of a good courage
